title: Repair C6e with Git-backed frozen Targets
goal: Repeat the bounded C6e production composition and installed Web UI practice on new paths using Git-backed detached worktrees at the certified Target commit.
acceptanceCriteria: Both new Target roots are detached Git worktrees whose HEAD is exactly the certified C6c Target commit.
A new production sibling installation and external composition receipt pass the public verifier.
Installed Web UI direct Pre passes on clean with non-vacuous coverage and blocks the deliberate IMPORT-DIRECTION violation.
UI verdicts, run IDs, findings, coverage and authority hashes match installed Host queries.
Protected inventories and expected Git facts are unchanged after practice.
The repair stops before P10.2 parity, P10.3 activation, publication, V3 retirement or IFX cutover.
risks: A worktree with the wrong HEAD would invalidate the certified Target identity.
Reusing a C6e path would confuse stopped and repaired execution evidence.
The deliberate violation could escape its one-file boundary or fail to produce blocking coverage.
C6e-R1 completion could be misrepresented as P10.2 parity or P10.3 activation.
decisions: Use two new detached Git worktrees rather than archive exports so workspace evidence can resolve HEAD.
Use a new sibling installation, receipt, StateRoot, EvidenceRoot and evidence directory.
Retain the stopped C6e execution unchanged and treat it only as the repair dependency.
